messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: multiple 5xx spikes (502/504) observed from gateway pool us-west2-edge starting ~1907654300. Paging: @Ryan (oncall), @Kevin T., @Maria S.. :rotating_light:

Maria S.: seeing ~40% 502 rate on /v1/generate proxied through us-west2-edge -> worker-pool-w2. Errors are mostly 'upstream reset' and occasional timeouts. Latency also spiking to 2-3s for requests that succeed.

Kevin T.: confirming from gateway logs — spikes aligned with high connection errors to worker-pool-w2. Possible partial AZ networking issue? Cloud provider shows increased packet loss in us-west2-a for NICs tied to pool.

Jess L.: any recent deploys?

Maria S.: no user-facing deploys in the last 3 hours. Canary looks clean.

ops-bot: Canary checksum: no new model rollout. Autoscaler reports pool at 85% utilization (target 70%).

Ryan (oncall): I'm on it. I'm going to isolate gateway -> pool traffic and fail traffic to fallback region for affected routes. Priority: reduce customer impact, keep <1% errors.

Maria S.: quick mitigation options:
- scale up worker-pool-w2 (add 4 nodes)
- temporarily route traffic for non-low-latency customers to eu-west1
- enable aggressive connection retries on gateway for 30s
- evict unhealthy nodes from pool

Kevin T.: I can add nodes but incurring burst. Can we confirm whether nodes are healthy but network-hosed or process-level OOMs?

Maria S.: stack traces show "read: connection reset by peer" and gateway metric shows TCP resets. No OOMs in process logs.

Jess L.: running a quick curl from us-west2-edge to one worker IP to reproduce:
```
curl -v http://10.12.78.45:8080/health
* Connected to 10.12.78.45 (10.12.78.45) port 8080 (#0)\n> GET /health HTTP/1.1\n> Host: 10.12.78.45:8080\n< HTTP/1.1 200 OK\n* Connection reset by peer\n* Closing connection 0\n```
We get intermittent resets.

Anna C.: CS: I'm getting messages from 3 paying customers in us-west region about errors. Collecting customer IDs and SLAs. Will post list in 10m.

Ryan (oncall): Plan: (1) start routing 30% of us-west2-edge traffic -> eu-west1 for non-geofenced customers; (2) enable retry/backoff at gateway (3 retries, 100ms backoff); (3) mark worker-pool-w2 nodes with >10% resets as drained, let autoscaler replace. Executing now.

Kevin T.: doing (1). Adding route override in routing-table: `route set us-west2-edge -> eu-west1 [path-preference=failover, weight=30%]`

ops-bot: Rollout started: route override applied to 12/16 gateway nodes.

Maria S.: enabling gateway retry config now:
```
gateway.config.retries = 3
gateway.config.retry_backoff_ms = 100
```

Maria S.: also toggled prefix-cache fallback to reduce re-compute for embeddings to 60s TTL.

Kevin T.: draining nodes flagged: removing 4 IPs from LB pool. Commands: `lb remove 10.12.78.{41,42,43,45}`.

Jess L.: after drain, error rate dropped from 42% -> 18% in 4m. Latency median improved 600ms -> 320ms.

Ryan (oncall): continuing to monitor. If error <5% in next 10m, keep partial failover. If not, escalate to full region failover.

Anna C.: customers impacted list so far: cust-845 (mid-size SaaS), cust-202 (finance sandbox), cust-930 (marketplace). All three affected with increased 5xx for API calls from us-west. CS has opened tickets and provided temporary guidance to route to eu-west (if feasible).

Maria S.: digging into networking: cloud provider reports degraded packet delivery between us-west2-a and internal gateway subnets for ~12m window. Looks like partial fabric issue.

Kevin T.: added temporary BGP path pin for gateway-to-worker traffic to prefer us-west2-b and us-west2-c subnets (if healthy) to avoid us-west2-a.

ops-bot: BGP pin applied across 16 gateways.

Jess L.: after BGP pin + drain, we're down to 6% 502s on impacted routes. Some customers still hit errors (likely long-lived conns).

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3451. Severity: Sev2. Owner: Ryan (oncall). Start: 1907654300.

Ryan (oncall): Doing on-call handoff note to morning shift in 20m. Leaving the active mitigation (route override + retries) in place. Who can own postmortem? Suggest Kevin and Maria.

Kevin T.: happy to pair on postmortem. I'll keep the routing override until fabric is 100% green.

Maria S.: I'll collect logs, KVs, and sample traces for the PM. Also will snapshot gateway metrics and pool membership at 1907654350.

Anna C.: CS: escalated to affected customers with ETA ~30m. Offering credits where SLAs breached. We'll follow up after RCA.

Ryan (oncall): Update: provider reports partial healing in us-west2-a; packet loss trending down. I'm going to slowly move traffic back (remove 10% failover every 5m).

ops-bot: Traffic rollback schedule: 30% -> 20% @1907654375 -> 10% @1907654380 -> 0% @1907654385

Jess L.: final check: 5xx now stable at 0.9% across all routes after last rollback. Latency back to baseline.

Maria S.: note for postmortem: root cause appears to be transient cloud fabric degradation in us-west2-a causing TCP resets; contributing factor: gateway's short connection retry policy and pool affinity kept sending traffic to affected AZ. Mitigations that helped: route failover, BGP pin, drain unhealthy nodes, and gateway retries.

Ryan (oncall): I'll mark the incident as 'stabilized' and handoff to Kevin for RCA + postmortem. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Anna C.: CS will follow up with customers once postmortem available.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-3451 status: STABILIZED at 1907654389.

Maria S.: leaving a couple of followups:
- Kevin: schedule PO for BGP pin automation to avoid manual steps
- Platform: consider auto-failover threshold for AZ-level fabric metrics
- SRE: build runbook for partial AZ fabric loss (include routing override commands and quick drain pattern)

Kevin T.: noted. I'll start a tracker and assign owners.

Ryan (oncall): logging final handoff to morning: everything stable, leaving notes in incident doc.

Jess L.: good job team.
